mainTopic: When executed people get כפרה; whether graves and items set aside for the dead become forbidden for benefit.
overview: The גמרא explains that people killed unjustly by a non-Jewish government get כפרה through their death, but people executed by a בית דין do not get it from death alone. They get it after death and burial, and, according to one answer, after their flesh decomposes. That is why their bones are moved to the family plot only after the flesh has decomposed. רב אשי gives a different answer: כפרה comes soon after burial, but the time for אבלות had already passed, so mourning is never started. Next comes a story about dirt taken from רב's grave as a cure for fever. שמואל allows it, because ground attached to the earth never becomes forbidden, and he learns this through a היקש from עבודה זרה. Three ברייתות seem to show graves becoming forbidden, and each is answered by saying it means a קבר בנין, a grave built from cut stones. Finally, אביי and רבא argue whether a garment woven for a dead person is forbidden. Their argument depends on whether הזמנה, setting something aside, counts. The גמרא begins to explain why רבא does not learn from עגלה ערופה, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Unjust deaths versus just executions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects comparing people killed by a non-Jewish government to people executed by a בית דין. The first group gets כפרה through death; the second group does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you compare people killed by the government to people killed by the court? People killed by the government are killed unjustly, so their death brings them atonement. People killed by the court are killed justly, so their death does not bring them atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on an earlier attempt to show that executed people get כפרה. It says the two kinds of killing cannot be compared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof used a פסוק in תהלים about Jews killed by enemies. Those victims die unjustly, so their death itself wipes away sin. Someone executed by בית דין is simply getting what the law calls for, so his death alone does not give him כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: People executed by a Jewish court

steps.confusionAlert: This line opens in the middle of a question. The words 'can you compare' come just before it, so read the whole line as a challenge to the comparison.

phrases.english: [Can you compare] those killed by the government to those killed by the court?
phrases.notes: The government victims are the ones in the פסוק in תהלים 79:2.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרוּגֵי מַלְכוּת, כֵּיוָן דְּשֶׁלֹּא בְּדִין קָא מִיקַּטְלִי,
phrases.english: Those killed by the government, since they are killed unjustly,
have atonement.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרוּגֵי בֵּית דִּין, כֵּיוָן דִּבְדִין קָא מִיקַּטְלִי,
phrases.english: Those killed by the court, since they are killed justly,
do not have atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made just before this section, between the victims in the פסוק and people executed by בית דין.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the פסוק about government victims as a proof about people executed by בית דין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An unjust death brings כפרה, but a just execution does not, so the two cases are different.

steps.title: Proof from not burying them with their ancestors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the claim from the משנה: executed people are not buried in their family graves. If execution gave them כפרה, they should be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is so, because we learned in the משנה: they would not bury him in his ancestors' graves. If you think that once they are executed they have atonement, let them be buried there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof that people executed by בית דין do not get כפרה from their death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the executed person is not buried in his family plot. The reasoning is: if his death had already cleansed him, nothing would stop him from lying next to his righteous relatives. So his death must not have given him כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Know (that this is true); it introduces a supporting proof
And if it enters your mind (if you were to think)

phrases.english: Know [that this is so], as we learned:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ קוֹבְרִין אוֹתוֹ בְּקִבְרוֹת אֲבוֹתָיו.
phrases.english: They would not bury him in his ancestors' graves.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the person executed by בית דין, from the earlier משנה.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind [to say],
that once they are killed they have atonement,
let them be buried [there]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from the משנה for Step 1's claim that execution by בית דין does not bring כפרה.
steps.raayaObject: That people executed by בית דין do not get כפרה from death alone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: they were not buried in their ancestors' graves.

steps.title: Death and burial are both needed
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed aside. Execution does lead to כפרה, but only once burial is added to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need death and burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proof. It says not burying him with his ancestors does not show that he never gets כפרה. It only shows that death alone is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כפרה comes in stages. He needs to die and also be buried, first in the special graves for executed people. So at the moment of death he cannot go straight into the family plot. This means executed people do get כפרה in the end, just not at the moment of death.

phrases.english: We need death and burial.
phrases.notes: He means both are needed before the executed person gets his כפרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof of Step 2 by adding burial as a condition for כפרה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that the burial rule proves there is no כפרה at all.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The burial rule only shows that death alone is not enough. Burial is also needed.

steps.title: רב אדא's challenge from the rules of mourning
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה objects from the משנה: relatives do not keep אבלות for an executed person. If burial gave him כפרה, they should mourn him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה objected: they would not observe mourning, but they would grieve, since grief is only in the heart. If you think that once they are buried they have atonement, let them observe mourning!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges the claim that death plus burial is enough for כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says relatives do not keep the outward mourning practices for an executed person. They only grieve privately in their hearts (אנינות). If he had already been cleansed by being buried, there would be no reason to hold back mourning.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava objected:
They would not mourn, but they would grieve,
since grief is only in the heart.
And if it enters your mind [to say],
that once they are buried they have atonement,
let them mourn!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 3's claim that death and burial are enough for כפרה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that death plus burial brings כפרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once someone has כפרה, he should be mourned normally. Since the משנה forbids normal mourning even after burial, burial must not have brought כפרה.

steps.title: The flesh must also decompose
steps.stepSummary: The answer: כפרה also requires עיכול בשר, the decomposition of the flesh, in addition to death and burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also need the flesh to decompose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אדא's challenge by adding one more stage before כפרה is complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Death and burial are not the last step. The flesh must also decompose. During the time of mourning the flesh has not yet decomposed, so he does not yet have full כפרה, and that is why there is no אבלות.
steps.whatToRemember: An executed person's כפרה comes in three stages: death, burial, and decomposition of the flesh.

phrases.english: We also need decomposition of the flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 4 by adding a third requirement for כפרה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a further condition (decomposition) to the process of כפרה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Death plus burial would be enough, so mourning should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: כפרה is complete only after the flesh decomposes, so there is no mourning before then.

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's wording backs this up: once the flesh decomposed, the bones were gathered and buried in their proper place. This shows decomposition completes the כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, since it teaches: once the flesh decomposed, they would gather the bones and bury them in their place. Learn from it that this is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה itself supports the idea that decomposition finishes the כפרה, and then it closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה times the move to the family plot exactly to when the flesh decomposed. That timing makes sense only if decomposition is what completes his כפרה. Once that happens, he may lie with his righteous relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise, the wording supports this
Learn from it (that this is so)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's timing of moving the bones to the family plot shows that decomposition completes the executed person's כפרה.

phrases.english: It is also precise, as it teaches:
Once the flesh has decomposed,
they gather the bones
and bury them in their place.
phrases.notes: 'Their place' means the family burial plot he couldn't be buried in at first.

phrases.english: Learn from it [that this is so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 5 from the wording of the משנה and closes the discussion.
steps.raayaObject: That decomposition of the flesh completes the כפרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: once the flesh decomposed, the bones were moved to their proper place.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A person executed by בית דין gets full כפרה only after death, burial, and decomposition of the flesh.

steps.title: רב אשי: mourning was missed at its start, so it stays missed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers רב אדא בר אהבה differently. אבלות begins at סתימת הגולל, but כפרה comes only after a little suffering in the grave. Since the moment for אבלות already passed, it is never started later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When does mourning begin? From the sealing of the grave cover. When does atonement happen? Once the dead person feels a little of the pain of the grave. So, since mourning was pushed off, it stays pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives another answer to the question of why relatives do not mourn an executed person. He points to a timing gap between when אבלות starts and when כפרה happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier answer, כפרה needed עיכול בשר. רב אשי says כפרה can come soon after burial, after a little צער הקבר. At the moment אבלות should have started, the person did not yet have כפרה. So אבלות was pushed off, and once it is pushed off it does not come back.

keyTerms.meaning: Mourning rites for a close relative
Sealing the grave with its cover stone, when mourning begins
Since they were pushed off, they stay pushed off

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the executed person never gets כפרה. He gets it soon after burial. The point is that אבלות was already skipped by then and is not restarted.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Mourning, from when does it begin?
From the sealing of the grave cover.
Atonement, from when does it happen?
From when they see a little of the pain of the grave.
phrases.notes: "They" means the dead people. Once they feel even a little of the grave's suffering, they already have כפרה.

phrases.english: Therefore, since they were pushed off, they stay pushed off.
phrases.notes: The mourning rites are what was pushed off. Their moment came before the כפרה did.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to רב אדא בר אהבה's question (step 4), different from the עיכול בשר answer in steps 5 and 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing distinction: when אבלות begins versus when כפרה is reached
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If burial brings כפרה, the relatives should mourn.
steps.terutzMaskana: כפרה comes only after a little צער הקבר, which is after סתימת הגולל. So the time for אבלות passed without it, and it is not restarted.

steps.title: If so, why wait for the flesh to decompose?
steps.stepSummary: If כפרה comes right after a little suffering in the grave, why does the משנה wait for עיכול בשר before moving the bones?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need the flesh to decompose?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי. If כפרה comes so early, why does the משנה wait until the flesh decomposes before reburying the bones in the family plot?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 read the משנה's wait for עיכול בשר as part of the כפרה. If רב אשי is right that כפרה comes much sooner, that wait seems to have no purpose.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, לְמָה לִי עִיכּוּל בָּשָׂר?
phrases.english: If so, why do I need decomposition of the flesh?
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה's rule that the bones go to the family grave only after the flesh decomposes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לְמָה לִי עִיכּוּל בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's answer from the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that כפרה comes soon after burial
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If כפרה comes early, waiting for עיכול בשר seems pointless.

steps.title: Waiting is practical, because the body cannot be moved earlier
steps.stepSummary: We wait for עיכול בשר not for כפרה, but because it is impossible to move the body before then.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wait has a practical reason, not a כפרה reason. The bones simply cannot be moved before the flesh decomposes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This changes how we read the משנה. The wait for עיכול בשר is a matter of what is physically possible, not a stage of כפרה. That keeps רב אשי's view standing.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: אבלות starts at סתימת הגולל, and כפרה comes a little later. Mourning that was pushed off stays pushed off. Waiting for עיכול בשר is only because the body cannot be moved before then.

phrases.english: Because it is not possible.
phrases.notes: He means it is not possible to gather and move the bones while the flesh is still on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reason instead of a legal one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Waiting for עיכול בשר is part of the כפרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wait is only because moving the bones earlier is not possible.

steps.title: Dirt from רב's grave used for fever, and שמואל allows it
steps.stepSummary: People took dirt from רב's grave as a cure for fever. שמואל said this is fine, because natural ground never becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: People would take dirt from רב's grave for a one-day fever. They came and told שמואל. He said: They are acting properly. It is natural ground, and natural ground does not become forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. People worried that dirt from a grave might be forbidden to use, and שמואל rules that it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that you may not get benefit from a grave. שמואל's rule is that קרקע עולם, ground in its natural state, is never forbidden. The grave dirt counts as that kind of ground. His source comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Natural ground that is still attached to the earth

phrases.aramaic: קִבְרֵיהּ דְּרַב הֲווֹ שָׁקְלִי מִינֵּיהּ עַפְרָא
phrases.english: From Rav's grave, they would take dirt
for a one-day fever.
They came and told Shmuel.
He said to them: They are acting properly,
it is natural ground,
and natural ground does not become forbidden,

steps.triggerLanguage: קִבְרֵיהּ דְּרַב הֲווֹ שָׁקְלִי מִינֵּיהּ עַפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about whether a grave is forbidden for benefit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Natural ground in a grave does not become forbidden, so its dirt may be used.

steps.title: A פסוק places graves next to עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל brings a פסוק where the dust of an אשרה is thrown on graves. This is a היקש comparing graves to עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And he cast its dust on the grave of the common people." The verse compares the grave of the common people to idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives his source. A פסוק mentions graves together with an idol, so the two are compared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק puts a grave and עבודה זרה side by side, whatever is true about which kinds of עבודה זרה become forbidden is also true of graves. The next step spells out what that rule is.

keyTerms.meaning: The grave of the common people
Compares one thing to another based on a פסוק (a היקש)

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ אֶת עֲפָרָהּ עַל קֶבֶר בְּנֵי הָעָם״,
phrases.english: As it is written: "And he cast its dust on the grave of the common people,"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 23:6. "Its dust" is the dust of the אשרה idol that was ground up.

phrases.aramaic: מַקִּישׁ קֶבֶר בְּנֵי הָעָם לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: It compares the grave of the common people to idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ אֶת עֲפָרָהּ עַל קֶבֶר בְּנֵי הָעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for שמואל's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: Natural ground in a grave does not become forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 23:6, a היקש between a grave and עבודה זרה

steps.title: Attached idols are not forbidden, so attached graves are not either
steps.stepSummary: עבודה זרה that is attached to the ground does not become forbidden, as we learn from "their gods upon the mountains". So a grave in attached ground is also not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as idol worship that is attached to the ground is not forbidden, as it is written: "whom you are dispossessing, their gods upon the high mountains". Their gods that are on the mountains must be destroyed, but not mountains that are their gods. Here too, what is attached does not become forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the comparison. First it proves that attached עבודה זרה is not forbidden, then it applies the same rule to the grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires destroying gods that stand "on" the mountains, not the mountains themselves even if they were worshipped. That shows ground that is attached does not become forbidden. Through the היקש, attached grave dirt is also not forbidden, so taking it is fine.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: ground that is attached and natural never becomes forbidden. This is learned through a היקש from עבודה זרה, where "their gods on the mountains" are destroyed but the mountains are not.
steps.confusionAlert: The mountain can still be a real object of עבודה זרה. The point is only that ground attached to the earth does not become forbidden to use.

phrases.aramaic: מָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בִּמְחוּבָּר לָא מִיתַּסְרָא,
phrases.english: Just as idol worship that is attached is not forbidden,
as it is written: "whom you are dispossessing,"
phrases.notes: דברים 12:2. This line is a side note showing where the עבודה זרה rule comes from.

phrases.english: "their gods upon the high mountains."
Their gods that are on the mountains must be destroyed,
but not mountains that are themselves their gods.
Here too, what is attached does not become forbidden.
phrases.notes: Back to the grave: its dirt is attached ground, so it is not forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בִּמְחוּבָּר לָא מִיתַּסְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the היקש from step 11 and applies it to graves.
steps.raayaObject: Attached grave ground is not forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 12:2, "their gods upon the mountains", not the mountains themselves
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Ground attached to the earth, including a grave, does not become forbidden, so dirt from רב's grave may be used.

steps.title: A grave dug for one's father becomes forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if a son dug a grave for his father but buried him somewhere else, the son may never be buried in that grave. This suggests a grave in the ground can become forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If someone digs a grave for his father, and then goes and buries him somewhere else, he may never be buried in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's rule that natural ground never becomes forbidden. It brings a ברייתא where a grave seems to become forbidden just from being dug for a dead person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said a grave in the ground cannot become אסור בהנאה. But this ברייתא forbids the son from using the grave he dug, even though nobody was ever buried in it. So it seems a grave in the ground can become forbidden after all.

keyTerms.meaning: One who digs or carves out

phrases.english: They challenged: One who digs a grave for his father,
and went and buried him in a different place –

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִקָּבֵר בּוֹ עוֹלָמִית.
phrases.english: he may never be buried in it.
phrases.notes: "He" is the son. The grave he made for his father is off-limits to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of steps 10-12 that a grave in natural ground cannot become forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that natural ground never becomes אסור בהנאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dug grave becomes forbidden to the son, so a grave attached to the ground can become forbidden.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a built grave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a קבר בנין, a grave built out of cut stones, and not a grave dug into the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A built grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by saying the ברייתא is about a different kind of grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קבר בנין is built from stones that were cut out of the ground and then put together. Those stones were once separated from the ground, so they can become forbidden. A plain grave dug into the earth still stays permitted, as שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
A grave built from stones above the ground

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying graves can never be forbidden. It is saying only a grave made from separated material can become forbidden, while one dug into natural ground cannot.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With a built grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about any grave, even one dug in the ground.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a built grave made of separated stones, so שמואל's rule stands.

steps.title: A new grave becomes forbidden once a stillborn is placed in it
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says a new grave is permitted, but once even a נפל is put in it, it becomes אסור בהנאה. This again suggests a grave can become forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A new grave is permitted for benefit. If a stillborn baby was placed in it, it is forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא to challenge שמואל again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא shows that a grave becomes forbidden as soon as a body is placed in it, even the body of a נפל. If this is any grave, then a grave in the ground can become forbidden, which goes against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby that was born unable to live

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: קֶבֶר חָדָשׁ מוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה.
phrases.english: Come and hear: A new grave is permitted for benefit.
If he placed a stillborn in it – it is forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against שמואל, after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that natural ground never becomes אסור בהנאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A grave becomes forbidden once a body is placed in it, which seems to include a grave in the ground.

steps.title: This too means a built grave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer: this ברייתא is also talking about a קבר בנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it means a built grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge the same way it answered the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a grave built from separated stones becomes forbidden when a body is placed in it. A grave dug into natural ground still does not become forbidden, so שמואל is not contradicted.

phrases.english: Here too, it is about a built grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 using the same answer as step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about any new grave.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about a built grave, so a dug grave stays permitted.

steps.title: Three kinds of graves: a known grave stays forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A third ברייתא lists three kinds of graves. A found grave may be cleared out, and its place is then pure and permitted. A known grave may not be cleared out, and even if it was, its place stays impure and forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: You find that there are three kinds of graves: a found grave, a known grave, and a grave that harms the public. A found grave may be cleared out. If he cleared it, its place is pure and permitted for benefit. A known grave may not be cleared out. If he cleared it, its place is impure and forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ברייתא to challenge שמואל. Here it starts quoting the ברייתא. The next step finishes it, and step 19 gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קבר הידוע is one source of the problem: even after the body is removed, its place stays forbidden. That sounds like the ground itself became forbidden, against שמואל. The next step adds a second case like this. The קבר הנמצא part is permitted, so it is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A grave that was found (buried without the owner's permission)
A known grave (buried with the owner's permission)
A grave that harms the public
To clear it out (move the body)

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge comes from the graves whose place stays forbidden: the קבר הידוע here, and the grave that harms the public in the next step. It does not come from the קבר הנמצא. The found grave is permitted, so it agrees with שמואל.

phrases.english: Come and hear: It turns out you say
there are three kinds of graves –
a found grave, a known grave,
and a grave that harms the public.
A found grave – one may clear it out.
If he cleared it – its place is pure and permitted for benefit.
A known grave – one may not clear it out.
If he cleared it – its place is impure and forbidden for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִמְצָא אַתָּה אוֹמֵר שָׁלֹשׁ קְבָרוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge against שמואל, after the first two were answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that natural ground never becomes אסור בהנאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The place of a known grave stays forbidden even after the body is removed, which suggests the ground itself became forbidden.

steps.title: The third grave: one that harms the public
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list. A grave that harms the public may be cleared out, and afterward its place is pure but still אסור בהנאה. This shows ground can become forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: A grave that harms the public may be cleared out. Once it is cleared, its place is pure but forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the third ברייתא from step 17. Its last case is another grave whose place stays forbidden even after the body is cleared out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after the body is taken out, the place of this grave stays אסור בהנאה. A place in the ground is attached to the ground, so this seems to show that something attached to the ground can become forbidden. That is exactly what the earlier answers tried to avoid.

keyTerms.meaning: A grave that harms the public
To clear it out (to move the body somewhere else)
Forbidden to get any benefit from

steps.confusionAlert: Being טהור and being אסור בהנאה are two separate things. A place can be pure, so it no longer makes people טמא, and still be forbidden to use or benefit from.

phrases.english: A grave that harms the public
may be cleared out.
Once he cleared it, its place is pure
but forbidden for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: קֶבֶר הַמַּזִּיק אֶת הָרַבִּים, מוּתָּר לְפַנּוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 17 and brings out its challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a grave dug in the ground does not become forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The cleared place of this grave stays אסור בהנאה, so a place in the ground can become forbidden.

steps.title: Again, it is a built grave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא is also talking about a קבר בנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is talking about a built grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the third ברייתא the same way it answered the first two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קבר בנין is made of stones that were cut and then built. It is not simply ground, so it can become forbidden. A grave dug into the ground still does not become forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A built grave, made of cut stones

steps.whatToRemember: All three ברייתות are answered the same way. Only a built grave becomes אסור בהנאה. A grave dug in the ground does not.

phrases.english: Here too, it is talking about a built grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 17–18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a particular case (a built grave).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about any grave, even one dug in the ground.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about a קבר בנין only, so ground-dug graves stay permitted.

steps.title: Maybe the found grave belongs to a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's rule that a found grave may be cleared out. Maybe it holds a מת מצוה, who acquires his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: May a found grave really be cleared out? Maybe it is a מת מצוה, and a מת מצוה acquires his place!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that it has quoted this ברייתא, the גמרא questions one of its details: the rule about a found grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מת מצוה is buried where he is found and may not be moved. If a found grave might belong to a מת מצוה, how can the ברייתא allow clearing it out?

keyTerms.meaning: A grave that is found (no one knew about it before)
A dead person with no one to bury him, so everyone must help bury him
Acquires his place (he must stay where he is buried)

phrases.english: And a found grave may be cleared out?
Maybe it is a מת מצוה,
and a מת מצוה acquires his place!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקֶבֶר הַנִּמְצָא מוּתָּר לְפַנּוֹתוֹ? דִּילְמָא מֵת מִצְוָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the main question and challenges a side detail of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a found grave may be cleared out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A found grave might belong to a מת מצוה, who may not be moved.

steps.title: A מת מצוה would be known
steps.stepSummary: A מת מצוה is different because people hear about him. So a found grave that no one knew about is not one.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מת מצוה is different, because he has publicity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we do not need to worry that a found grave holds a מת מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a מת מצוה is buried, word gets around and people know where he is. If no one knew about this grave, it is not a מת מצוה, so it may be cleared out.

keyTerms.meaning: A voice, meaning publicity or rumor

phrases.english: A מת מצוה is different,
because he has publicity.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי מֵת מִצְוָה, דְּקָלָא אִית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual answer: such a case would be publicly known.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any found grave might hold a מת מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מת מצוה's burial becomes known, so a grave no one knew about is not one.

steps.title: A garment woven for a dead person
steps.stepSummary: A new מחלוקת: if someone weaves a garment for a dead person, אביי says it is forbidden and רבא says it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: one who weaves a garment for a dead person — אביי says it is forbidden, and רבא says it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new disagreement between אביי and רבא about a garment made for the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a garment made for a dead person but never actually used for him. The question is whether making it for the dead already makes it אסור בהנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A garment for a dead person (a shroud)

phrases.english: It was said: one who weaves a garment for a dead person —
אביי says: it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: He means forbidden to benefit from, even though it was never put on the dead person.

phrases.english: and רבא says: it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about things made for the dead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: a garment woven for the dead is אסור בהנאה. רבא: it is permitted.

steps.title: The reasons: does designation count?
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds that הזמנה counts, so the garment is forbidden. רבא holds that הזמנה does not count, so the garment is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says forbidden, because designating something counts. רבא says permitted, because designating something does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each side of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, setting the garment aside for the dead is already enough to forbid it. For רבא, nothing changes until the garment is actually used on the dead person.

keyTerms.meaning: Designation, setting something aside for a use
Is nothing (it has no legal effect)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole מחלוקת comes down to one question: does הזמנה alone change something's status? אביי says yes. רבא says no, only actual use does.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of הזמנה goes beyond this one case. It is a general question that can come up wherever something is set aside for a purpose.

phrases.english: אביי says forbidden —
designation is something.
And רבא says permitted —
designation is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר אָסוּר – הַזְמָנָה מִלְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the מחלוקת in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disagreement depends on whether הזמנה has legal effect: אביי says it does, רבא says it does not.

steps.title: אביי's source: learning from עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns the word "שָׁם" by a dead person from the word "שָׁם" by an עגלה ערופה. Since an עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden through designation, so does a garment made for a dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is אביי's reason? He compares the word "there" used for a grave to the word "there" used for the עגלה ערופה. Just as the עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden as soon as it is set aside, items for a dead person also become forbidden as soon as they are set aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where אביי gets his rule that designation makes something forbidden. It answers with a גזירה שוה from עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word "שָׁם" appears by מרים's burial and by the עגלה ערופה. A גזירה שוה links the two topics so they share a law. An עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden from the moment it is chosen for the מצוה, so for אביי the garment woven for the dead is forbidden right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Comparing two topics because the same word appears in both
The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown

steps.confusionAlert: Both אביי and רבא use the very same word "שָׁם". They do not argue about whether to compare. They argue about which topic to compare the dead person to.

phrases.english: What is the reason of אביי?
He learns "there" "there" from the עגלה ערופה.
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים are במדבר 20:1 (מרים was buried there) and דברים 21:4 (the calf's neck is broken there).

phrases.english: Just as an עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden through designation,
this too becomes forbidden through designation.
phrases.notes: "This" means the garment woven for the dead person from Step 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for אביי's view that הזמנה counts, from Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of "שָׁם" "שָׁם" from עגלה ערופה, which becomes forbidden through designation.

steps.title: רבא's source: learning from עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns the word "שָׁם" by a dead person from the word "שָׁם" by עבודה זרה. Since עבודה זרה does not become forbidden through designation alone, neither does a garment for the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא compares the word "there" used for a grave to the word "there" used for idol worship. Just as idol items do not become forbidden just by setting them aside, items for a dead person also do not become forbidden just by setting them aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבא's source. He uses the same word, but compares it to עבודה זרה instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With עבודה זרה, an item becomes forbidden only once it is actually worshipped, not just set aside for worship. רבא applies that to the dead. So the garment becomes forbidden only once it is actually used for the dead person, not when it is woven.

keyTerms.meaning: Designation, setting something aside for a purpose

steps.whatToRemember: אביי compares the dead to עגלה ערופה, so designation forbids. רבא compares the dead to עבודה זרה, so designation does not forbid. Both use the word "שָׁם".

phrases.english: And רבא learns "there" "there" from idol worship.

phrases.aramaic: מָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּהַזְמָנָה לָא מִיתַּסְרָא,
phrases.english: Just as idol worship does not become forbidden through designation,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הָכָא נָמֵי בְּהַזְמָנָה לָא מִיתַּסְרָא.
phrases.english: so too here, it does not become forbidden through designation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite source for רבא, next to אביי's source in Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of "שָׁם" "שָׁם" from עבודה זרה, which does not become forbidden through designation.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבא learn from עגלה ערופה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא chooses עבודה זרה and not עגלה ערופה, and starts to give his answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא, why doesn't he learn from the עגלה ערופה? He could tell you:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: why did he skip the comparison that אביי used? The words "אמר לך" set up רבא's answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the word "שָׁם" points to both topics, רבא needs a reason to reject the עגלה ערופה comparison. The question is opened here, and the answer continues in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (introduces how a sage would defend his view)

phrases.english: And רבא, what is the reason
that he does not learn from the עגלה ערופה?
He could say to you:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא גָּמַר מֵעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's choice of source from Step 25 in light of אביי's source in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's choice to learn from עבודה זרה instead of עגלה ערופה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word "שָׁם" also appears by עגלה ערופה, so רבא needs a reason not to learn from it.
